paper_title: Self-Interpretability LLMs Can Describe Complex Internal Processes that   Drive Their Decisions, and Improve with Training
caption: Results of Experiments 1 and 2. GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini can accurately report quantitative factors driving their decision-making across a great variety of scenarios, and fine-tuning on accurate explanation further improves their ability to do so. Left: Models were making choices based on preferences instilled in them by fine-tuning. Each point corresponds to a single attribute (e.g., condo ceiling height; 5 per choice contexts, 100 choice contexts). Location in the x-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model assigned to an attribute (as reflected in their decisions). Location in the y-dimension corresponds to the weight that a model reported assigning to that attribute when prompted explicitly. The weights the models reported meaningfully correlated with the weights that actually guided their decisions, and fine-tuning on examples of accurate reports further improved their accuracy. Right: The Pearson correlation between the models' reported and learned attribute weights before and after training (blue and purple, respectively). The reports of the base models that had not undergone this fine-tuning were almost entirely uncorrelated with the learned preferences (gray). Thus, the accuracy of the fine-tuned models must reflect their ability to report their new (fine-tuned) preferences and not an informed guess about their preferences based on their general background knowledge. Error bars indicate 95% HDIs.

model_annotations.Chinese: This vertical bar chart displays the Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences) for two different AI models across three experimental conditions. The horizontal category axis presents the models, labeled "GPT-4o" and "GPT-4o-mini," positioned from left to right. The vertical value axis is labeled "Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences)" and uses a linear numerical scale that ranges from exactly 0.00 to 1.00, marked with uniform tick intervals every 0.25; the axis baseline extends slightly below zero to accommodate a negative value and error bar. The chart features grouped bars, where three distinct bars are clustered side-by-side for each of the two horizontal categories. A legend in the upper-left corner explains the color coding for these groupings: a light gray bar denotes the "Control" condition, a light blue bar indicates "Before Introspection Training," and a dark purple bar represents "After Introspection Training." In the "GPT-4o" group, the light gray Control bar has a value of approximately 0.10, the light blue Before Introspection Training bar is roughly 0.54, and the dark purple After Introspection Training bar reaches about 0.74. In the "GPT-4o-mini" group, the chart displays the shortest bar with the light gray Control bar dipping slightly below the axis line to approximately -0.01. Its corresponding light blue bar is near 0.51, and the dark purple bar represents the highest value on the chart at approximately 0.75. The main categories on the horizontal axis are not sorted by numerical or alphabetical order, but the bars within each group consistently follow the same left-to-right sequence of Control, Before, and After training. Additionally, every bar in the chart is visually annotated with a gray vertical error bar featuring capped ends to indicate data variability.
model_annotations.English: This grouped vertical bar chart illustrates the Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences) for two models, GPT-4o and GPT-4o-mini, across three training conditions. The horizontal axis categorizes the data by model, displaying "GPT-4o" on the left and "GPT-4o-mini" on the right. The vertical axis measures the numerical values, labeled "Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences)", using a linear scale that ranges from 0.00 to 1.00 with major tick marks at regular intervals of 0.25. The chart features a grouped arrangement where each model category contains a cluster of three adjacent vertical bars corresponding to conditions defined in the top-left legend: grey for "Control", light blue for "Before Introspection Training", and dark purple for "After Introspection Training". Every bar is visually annotated with a vertical grey error bar with horizontal caps. Within the GPT-4o group, the grey Control bar is at approximately 0.10, the light blue Before Introspection Training bar is roughly 0.54, and the dark purple After Introspection Training bar is about 0.74. For the GPT-4o-mini group, the grey Control bar is the shortest overall, dropping slightly below the zero baseline to roughly -0.01, the light blue Before Introspection Training bar reaches approximately 0.51, and the dark purple After Introspection Training bar is the tallest on the chart at approximately 0.75. The bars within each group are not sorted by ascending or descending height, but instead follow a consistent order reflecting the legend's sequence of training conditions.
model_annotations.German: Das Diagramm stellt die Genauigkeit der Selbsteinschätzung bezüglich implementierter Präferenzen von zwei verschiedenen Modellen dar. Die horizontale Kategorieachse zeigt die Modelle „GPT-4o“ und „GPT-4o-mini“, die nebeneinander von links nach rechts angeordnet sind. Die vertikale Werteachse ist linear skaliert, trägt die Beschriftung „Self-Report Accuracy (Instilled Preferences)“ und weist einen Wertebereich von 0.00 bis 1.00 auf, wobei die numerischen Markierungen in regelmäßigen Intervallen von 0.25 (0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00) gesetzt sind. Das Diagramm verwendet gruppierte vertikale Balken, wobei für jede Modellkategorie drei Balken direkt nebeneinander stehen. Gemäß der Legende in der oberen linken Ecke repräsentiert die hellgraue Farbe die Bedingung „Control“, die hellblaue Farbe „Before Introspection Training“ und die dunkellila Farbe „After Introspection Training“. In der Gruppe für „GPT-4o“ liegt der hellgraue Kontrollbalken bei einem ungefähren Wert von 0.10, der hellblaue Balken bei etwa 0.54 und der dunkellila Balken bei ca. 0.74. In der Gruppe für „GPT-4o-mini“ weist der hellgraue Kontrollbalken mit etwa -0.01 den niedrigsten Wert des gesamten Diagramms auf und ragt leicht unter die Basislinie von 0.00. Der zugehörige hellblaue Balken erreicht einen Wert von ca. 0.51, und der dunkellila Balken zeigt mit etwa 0.75 den höchsten Wert des Diagramms. Es ist ein konsistentes visuelles Muster erkennbar, bei dem in beiden Modellgruppen der hellgraue Balken am kürzesten und der dunkellila Balken am höchsten ist. Die Balken sind nicht nach Größe oder Alphabet sortiert, sondern folgen innerhalb jeder Gruppe von links nach rechts der vorgegebenen Reihenfolge der Legende. Zur visuellen Hervorhebung ist jeder Balken im oberen Bereich mit einem schmalen grauen, vertikalen Fehlerbalken versehen, der mit horizontalen Kappen abschließt und sich sowohl nach oben als auch nach unten über den angezeigten Hauptwert hinaus erstreckt.
